title: Feedback strata and probe notebook (compact)
content:
Sprint-ready compact synthesis for field feedback (working notes)

Goal / context
- Short synthesis of recent CS + SRE + Solutions intake (Jul 2026) focused on inference economics and runtime friction. Aim: convert recurring asks into probeable experiments and a 6-week needle list for Optimize.
- Audience: product-optimize, solutions-engineering, and on-call runtime SMEs. This is intentionally lightweight — treat as scratchpad for next sync.

Topline findings (one-liners)
1) Customers ask for clearer controls that trade latency <-> cost without deep infra changes (UI + API knobs).
2) KV/prefix caching surprises are a primary cause of perceived instability in latency-sensitive flows. Many teams workaround with brittle client logic.
3) Rollout fallback ergonomics (automatic variant fallback + transparent metrics) repeatedly requested by mid-market customers.
4) Embedding / reranking quality regressions are sticky — customers want signal-level evals tied to rollouts.
5) Billing surprises from autoscale spikes (burst vs reserved) are a trust issue; need quick visibility + soft limits.

Representative customer snippets (raw)
- "Our latency spiked mid-day and our fallback to smaller model returned nonsense — we had to revert code." — FinSearch Ops
- "We tried prefix caching but the docs were fuzzy; our app got stale outputs because we misread TTL semantics." — HealthMap Eng
- "If we could pre-declare an acceptable p50/p95 tradeoff and let Redwood tune batching, we'd pay for it." — EdTech product manager

Synthesis: themes and root causes
A. Operability: fallback + rollout transparency
- Problem: rollouts that silently downgrade model family or quantization break semantics. Customers want visible policy simulation and safe fallbacks that preserve functional guarantees (e.g., same API schema + deterministic fallback label).
- Root cause: opaque routing and model-variant mappings; lack of route-level testing harness.

B. Cost/latency primitives (controls + observability)
- Problem: teams want simple declarative knobs (e.g., target_latency_ms, max_cost_per_1000_tokens) without hand-crafting batching and cache policies.
- Root cause: current surface exposes low-level knobs (batch size, cache TTL) but not high-level economic intents.

C. KV/prefix cache UX and semantics
- Problem: misunderstanding TTLs, prefix scope, and cache warming; edge-cases when model weight/quantization changes cause cache invalidation surprises.
- Root cause: mixing cache semantics across hosted and private deployments; docs fragmented across Console and API reference.

D. Quality safety and eval linkage
- Problem: customers lose confidence when a model update improves cost but degrades reranking/precision. They want prompt-set tied quality gates in rollouts.
- Root cause: model onboarding pipeline lacks customer-visible eval artifacts and easy binding to canary thresholds.

E. Billing & bursting transparency
- Problem: unexpected burst charges and reserved-capacity interactions cause churn risk. Customers ask for pre-flight burst simulations and soft spend caps.
- Root cause: billing telemetry is lagged and not joined to request-level routing decisions in Console.

Probe ideas (quick experiments, 1–6 week horizon)
1) Declarative SLO control (spike): create a route-level JSON manifest with target_latency_ms and max_cost_ms_per_token; runtime returns a confidence band and suggested kernel/policy. Quick UI prototype + API flag. (JIRA OPT-5123)
   - Success signal: 3 pilot customers able to set SLO and reduce queries to support by 20%.

2) Rollout simulation UI (spike): Console shows an offline simulation of a rollout policy — for a given traffic sample, show % calls routed to each variant, expected p50/p95, and which requests would have fallen back. Minimal: use last 24h sample.
   - Success: decreased rollback incidents in pilot accounts.

3) Cache semantics doc sprint + TTL visualizer (2 wks): one-page canonical doc + Console visualizer showing cache hit/miss by prefix over sample traffic and a TTL simulator. Pair with one engineering runbook for private customers.
   - Success: fewer KV cache support tickets and clearer doc metrics.

4) Canary eval binding (4 wks): wire prompt-set evals into rollout flows — when a canary deploy occurs, run the eval harness and block promotion if key metrics drop beyond threshold. Provide diff view.
   - Success: customers report higher trust; pilot team signs off.

5) Burst preview + soft cap (6 wks): create a simulation tool to show estimated costs for expected burst profile and an opt-in soft cap that attenuates throughput (and returns 429s with clear messaging) before hard charges apply.
   - Success: reduce billing disputes for pilot customers.

Prioritization sketch (subjective)
- Low friction / high impact: Cache doc sprint, Rollout simulation UI spike.
- Medium: Declarative SLO control prototype.
- Higher effort: Canary eval binding, Burst preview + soft cap (needs billing + infra changes).

Concrete mini backlog (actions for next 2 weeks)
- A1: Draft Console mock for rollout simulation (owner: Priya). Deliverables: 2 slides + JSON sample feed. Due: 2026-08-18.
- A2: Short canonical doc + TTL visualizer spec (owner: Diego). Deliverables: doc draft + example curl. Due: 2026-08-10.
- A3: Identify 3 pilot customers for Declarative SLO (owner: Liam). Deliverables: pilot agreement email templates. Due: 2026-08-14.
- A4: Wire OPT-5123 to product roadmap draft and add initial acceptance criteria (owner: Ava). Due: 2026-08-09.

Open questions / risks (notes to self)
- How opinionated should declarative SLOs be? (Fully managed tuning vs suggestions only) — impacts SLO liability and support load.
- Can we simulate burst costs without access to customers' reserved contracts? (may need billing data join).
- KV cache invalidation on quantization: do we need a cross-team signal when model variant changes to invalidate caches? (engineering change + migration plan).

Metrics to watch if we run probes
- Support ticket volume for KV cache issues (baseline + post-probe).
- Rollback rate for production model updates among pilot accounts.
- Number of billing disputes / spike-related tickets.
- Customer-reported trust score (simple 1–5 survey) for pilot cohort.

Stakeholder mapping
- Owners: product-optimize (Ava), solutions-eng (Liam), docs (Diego), runtime infra (TBD SRE lead).
- Pilot customers: shortlist candidate: FinSearch, HealthMap, EdTech (ask CS to intro).

Notes / fragments for next doc version
- Add small table mapping each ask to required infra changes (routing, cache metadata, billing joins).
- Quick reference: recommended default TTLs and examples for common patterns (chat assistant, search rerank, embeddings store).
- Consider a lightweight SDK helper for cache warm/warmup semantics.

References and raw inputs

- Customer email excerpts (redacted) — attached in JIRA OPT-5123
- Prior experiments: rollout-canary-diff (github PR#782)

Status / next sync
